thesis.summary: Only US-owned enricher; sole domestic HALEU source. Profitable, strategically irreplaceable.

catalyst.text: $900M HALEU task-order definitive agreement; enrichment capacity expansion

thesis.bull: The only US-owned-and-operated uranium enrichment company and the first to produce HALEU from a US-licensed centrifuge cascade — putting Centrus at the center of the advanced-reactor fuel supply chain with strong, bipartisan government backing as the West de-risks dependence on Russian enrichment.
thesis.bear: HALEU demand is contingent on advanced reactors actually deploying on schedule; reactor timelines historically slip, which would starve the thesis of revenue. Scaling enrichment is extremely capital-intensive, and a large share of near-term revenue depends on continued government funding.
invalidationConditions: The DOE HALEU program is cancelled, defunded, or not renewed
A competitor obtains a US license to enrich HALEU at commercial scale
Advanced-reactor deployment timelines slip materially across the major customers
unknowns: Long-term customer concentration beyond US government programs is unclear
Capex required to reach commercial HALEU scale is not fully defined
Timeline for cascade scale-up to commercial enrichment volume is unproven

evidence.claim: First to produce HALEU from a US-licensed centrifuge cascade (Piketon, OH)
Operates under DOE HALEU Availability Program contracts
Enrichment is a physical centrifuge-cascade process, not a software-replaceable capability
